title: Symphony No. 4 in A major, “Italian”
hook: A young traveller’s Italy in four movements, from sunlit opening to a whirling Roman dance.

painting.title: The Arrival of the Harvesters in the Pontine Marshes
painting.pairingNote: Harvesters arriving with an ox cart under a clear sky south of Rome, painted in the year Mendelssohn reached Italy; the same bright, festive Italy that the symphony’s outer movements celebrate.

facts: Mendelssohn spent 1830 and 1831 travelling, and from the autumn of 1830 he was in Italy: Venice, Florence, Rome, Naples. He began a symphony there. In February 1831 he wrote to his sister Fanny from Rome that it would be “the jolliest piece I have ever done, especially the last movement”.
He finished it in Berlin on 13 March 1833 for the Philharmonic Society of London, and conducted the first performance in London on 13 May 1833. He was 24.

He was never satisfied with it. He revised the last three movements in 1834 and never published the symphony. It appeared only in 1851, four years after his death, which is why it carries a higher number than works written after it.

There is no folk music in the first three movements. The finale is the exception: it borrows the leaping saltarello of Rome and the whirling tarantella of Naples. It also does something rare for a symphony of its time: it begins in A major and ends in A minor.
bigPicture.inOneLine: sunlight and speed (I), a grave procession (II), a gentle dance with distant horns (III), a breathless Roman dance in the minor (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: The symphony starts at full speed: quick repeated chords in the woodwinds, and the violins leap in with a wide, bright tune. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]], with a gentle second theme and a surprise in the middle: a new, nervous little tune that the instruments pass between them in strict imitation.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, violins
mainIdeas.description: a wide, leaping tune in a quick, skipping rhythm over chattering woodwind chords.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, clarinets and bassoons
mainIdeas.description: a smooth, gentle melody that moves in small steps.

mainIdeas.name: The new theme
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, clipped figure in the minor that appears only in the middle of the movement.

stops.hear: Flutes, oboes, clarinets and horns tap out quick repeated chords; the violins spring in with a high, leaping tune
stops.happening: Theme 1, in A major. The woodwinds’ patter keeps going underneath

stops.hear: The whole orchestra takes up the tune, loud and full
stops.happening: The theme in [[tutti|tutti]], then a busy passage that moves away from home

stops.hear: The music softens; clarinets and bassoons sing a smooth, stepwise melody
stops.happening: Theme 2, in E major

stops.hear: A quiet passage winds down, and the opening tune starts again from the beginning
stops.happening: The repeat of the [[exposition|exposition]]. Mendelssohn writes a special lead-back, whose figures return later

stops.hear: Hushed and in the minor: the strings play a short, clipped tune, and the other instruments enter one after another with the same tune
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] opens with a new theme treated as a [[fugato|fugato]]

stops.hear: The new tune and pieces of Theme 1 are combined; the music grows very quiet over a long-held note, then swells
stops.happening: The long approach to the return

stops.hear: The opening tune bursts back in the home key
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The clipped tune from the development returns, now urgent and loud
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]] brings back the new theme

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Theme 1 rings out over the whole orchestra; quick, emphatic final chords
stops.happening: The movement ends in a blaze of A major

notice: Listen to the woodwinds’ repeated chords under the opening tune. They keep up a steady patter for minutes, like a pulse.
The new tune in the middle of the movement is easy to miss on first hearing. Once you know it, listen for it again near the end, where it drives the coda.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Abbado recorded the symphony with the London Symphony Orchestra in October 1984, in St John’s Smith Square, London. He plays the repeat of the opening section, which is why the first movement lasts over ten minutes. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 1–4, followed by the “Reformation” Symphony.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: A slow, steady walk in D minor. A grave melody, sung by oboe, bassoon and violas together, moves over a bass line that never stops walking. It is often heard as a procession of pilgrims, and tradition links it to religious processions Mendelssohn saw in Italy. Twice the clarinets bring a warmer, major-key song, and at the end the procession passes into the distance.

mainIdeas.name: The call
mainIdeas.description: a short, wailing figure for winds and violas, heard at the very start and again at the end.

mainIdeas.name: The march
mainIdeas.description: a plain, chant-like melody over evenly walking notes in the cellos and basses.

mainIdeas.name: The episode
mainIdeas.description: a gentler, rising tune for clarinets in the major.

stops.hear: A short, wailing call, then silence
stops.happening: The opening call, played by woodwinds and violas in [[unison|unison]]

stops.hear: Oboe, bassoon and violas sing a grave, chant-like melody; underneath, the cellos and basses walk in short, even notes
stops.happening: The march theme, in D minor

stops.hear: The violins take over the melody, and two flutes weave a line above it
stops.happening: The march repeated with a new upper voice

stops.hear: The mood lifts: the clarinets sing a warmer, rising tune
stops.happening: A contrasting episode in A major

stops.hear: The march returns, with the walking bass underneath
stops.happening: The opening music comes back, shortened

stops.hear: The clarinets’ warm tune returns, now in D major
stops.happening: The episode comes back in the home key’s major

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The melody breaks off; the walking bass goes on alone, softer and softer, and the call returns
stops.happening: The procession fades into the distance

notice: Follow the bass. It walks at the same steady pace from the first bars to the last, even when the melody stops.

movements.heading: Con moto moderato
movements.summary: Not a fast scherzo but an unhurried dance in three, close to an old-fashioned [[minuet|minuet]]. Its long, smooth melody flows from the strings into the woodwinds. In the middle, the [[trio|trio]], two horns and bassoons play a soft fanfare, as if from far away.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a long, smooth string melody in A major, warm and a little wistful.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: quiet horn calls, answered by quick, light figures in the violins and flutes.

stops.hear: The violins play a long, flowing melody at an easy pace
stops.happening: The dance, in A major

stops.hear: The woodwinds take part, and the melody spreads through the orchestra
stops.happening: The second half of the dance

stops.hear: Two horns and bassoons play a soft, rounded fanfare
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]], in E major

stops.hear: Violins and flutes answer with quick, light figures; the horn calls grow louder, then fade
stops.happening: The trio rises to a brief climax

stops.hear: The flowing melody returns
stops.happening: The dance again, with new details in the accompaniment

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The horn calls come back quietly; the movement ends softly
stops.happening: A [[coda|coda]] that remembers the trio

notice: In the trio, listen for the horns and bassoons together: a soft, rounded sound, like a call heard across a valley.

movements.heading: Saltarello: Presto
movements.summary: A dance that never stops for breath. Its title is the saltarello, a jumping dance from Rome, and later Mendelssohn adds the smooth, whirling patter of the Neapolitan tarantella. The music stays in the minor almost to the end and finishes in A minor, not in the A major where the symphony began.

mainIdeas.description: The [[saltarello|saltarello]]: a leaping tune in a hopping, three-note rhythm, first on the flutes.
The [[tarantella|tarantella]]: an unbroken stream of quick notes that winds up and down in the strings.

stops.hear: Loud, abrupt chords from the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The introduction

stops.hear: Two flutes play a leaping tune in a hopping rhythm, over light strings
stops.happening: The [[saltarello|saltarello]] theme, in A minor

stops.hear: The violins and then the whole orchestra take up the dance
stops.happening: The tune spreads, louder and fuller

stops.hear: Quieter: a smooth, unbroken stream of quick notes winds through the violins
stops.happening: The [[tarantella|tarantella]], the second dance

stops.hear: The two dances are thrown together and pushed through new keys; short bursts of the leaping tune
stops.happening: The middle of the movement, where the ideas are worked

stops.hear: The flutes’ leaping tune returns
stops.happening: The opening dance comes back

stops.hear: Very quiet: the stream of quick notes sinks low and almost disappears
stops.happening: The calm before the last surge

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A sudden build to full volume and hard, final chords in A minor
stops.happening: The symphony ends in the minor

notice: Listen for the notes grouped in threes under the flute tune. That restless triple patter runs through almost the whole movement.
Compare the last chord with the first chord of the symphony. The key is the same, A, but the major has turned to minor.

threads.title: Light and shade
threads.body: The outer movements are bright and fast; the middle two are grave and gentle. Many writers hear the middle movements as more “northern” in mood, less Italian than the outer ones.

threads.title: Never finished
threads.body: Mendelssohn conducted the symphony only at its premiere and then kept revising it. The version heard almost everywhere today is the one he first performed in 1833.

threads.title: Woodwinds
threads.body: From the patter of the opening to the flutes’ saltarello, the woodwinds carry much of the symphony’s colour.
